messages:
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for rl-service v2.3.1 -> prod (canary=10%)
deploy-bot: Config change: rate-limiter.rules updated (applied via infra/rl-service/2026-03-15-canary) :rocket:

incident-bot: PAGER: High error rate detected on /v1/generate (prod-us-east). 429 spike > 30s threshold. Severity: P2. Paging @oncall_ryan and eng-sre.

Ryan (oncall): acknowledged. pulling metrics now — @Maya can you join?

Maya (eng-sre): on it. I see a sudden surge in 429s at 1798504118 -> correlates exactly with deploy timestamp. Top source: internal token accounting calls and a handful of customer tokens. Looks like exemptions are not being honored.

Tom (eng-runtime): checking canary logs. seeing this in rl-rate-limiter logs:
```
2026-03-15T14:02:58Z ERROR ratelimit: token_exemptions_lookup failed for namespace "redwood-system": key not found
2026-03-15T14:03:01Z WARN ratelimit: rejecting request single_token=abc123 user=svc-ingress reason=overflow
```

Maya (eng-sre): That token_exemptions lookup failure is new — likely schema change in rules. The canary's rule parser may have tightened validation and dropped exemptions that used to be wildcarded.

Priya (support): Getting multiple 429 reports from customers: AcmeCorp (TCK-2345), BrightDB (TCK-2346). Both reporting degraded throughput and some timeouts. Tickets opened.

Anika (product): How widespread? we need scope for comms.

Maya (eng-sre): 10% canary nodes show ~45% of their requests as 429s. Non-canary nodes are normal so far. Canary routing = 10% of traffic so roughly 8-12% customer impact depending on routing.

Ryan (oncall): immediate mitigation options? rollback canary, flip feature flag, or apply a quick patch to parser. Which is fastest?

Tom (eng-runtime): Easiest is kill the new rule parsing path via feature flag or rollback the canary deployment to v2.3.0. Rollback will restore previous binary and rules. Feature flag flip is faster if the flag exists.

deploy-engineer: deploy system shows a feature flag "rl_canary_new_rule_parser" enabled for canary. we can toggle it off to force old parser.

Ryan (oncall): Toggle it. Post the command you run.

deploy-engineer: running toggle now:
```
# internal flags service
curl -s -X POST https://flags.internal/api/toggle \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${FLAGS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{"flag":"rl_canary_new_rule_parser","env":"prod","value":false}'
```

ops-bot: Action logged: flag rl_canary_new_rule_parser set to false by deploy-engineer at 2026-03-15T14:05:22Z

Maya (eng-sre): watching metric streams... rate of 429s dropping on canary nodes within 30s. good sign.

Tom (eng-runtime): rolling metrics:
- 14:03:00 -> 14:05:00 canary 429s peaked at 320 rps
- 14:06:00 -> 14:07:00 canary 429s down to 18 rps

Priya (support): AcmeCorp confirms improved throughput, closing emergency note on their ticket (TCK-2345). BrightDB still saw errors but much reduced.

Ryan (oncall): Great. So mitigation = feature flag flip. Root cause looks like the new rule parser dropped exemptions due to stricter schema. We need a rollback of the canary or a patch?

Tom (eng-runtime): Patch will take ~2-3 hours to validate. We should rollback the canary rollout to be safe and then patch in staging. I'll coordinate rollback.

deploy-bot: Canary rollback initiated for rl-service -> revert to v2.3.0 (canary=0%).

deploy-engineer: rollback complete at 2026-03-15T14:12:19Z. Verified pods at v2.3.0 across canary group.

Maya (eng-sre): Monitoring shows sustained low 429s now. Full health checks passing.

Anika (product): Noting customer impact: two customers had degraded experience for ~8 minutes (peak window). We should prepare a short comms note: timeline, impact, mitigation.

Priya (support): Drafting customer note and will tie to ticket numbers. cc: SRE and Product for review.

Ryan (oncall): Initial incident timeline:
- 14:02:58Z deploy canary v2.3.1 (rule parser change)
- 14:03:10Z 429 spike detected by incident-bot (auto)
- 14:04:30Z oncall paged and triage started
- 14:05:22Z feature flag rl_canary_new_rule_parser toggled OFF -> immediate improvement
- 14:12:19Z canary rollback to v2.3.0 completed
- 14:15:00Z monitoring green, customer confirmations received

Maya (eng-sre): postmortem action items:
- Fix parser schema handling and add unit tests for exemptions (owner: Tom)
- Add regression test that simulates exemption wildcarding (owner: eng-ml?)
- Add a canary-safety check that validates exemption counts before switching parser (owner: Maya)
- Add alert rule to correlate deploys and sudden config key drops (owner: SRE)

Tom (eng-runtime): will open a PR with the schema fix and start validation run.

Priya (support): I'll publish customer comms draft in #customer-notices and link to tickets.

Ryan (oncall): Leaving this thread to record final notes. Will file incident in pagerduty with severity P2 and assign postmortem. Thanks all for quick response. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident ticket PD-7891 created and assigned to Ryan (oncall).

Maya (eng-sre): tagging this for follow-up in postmortems; will add logs/metrics snapshot to the incident doc.

Anika (product): schedule 1-hour recap tomorrow 10:00 for learnings and comms alignment.

---
Post-incident quick notes: affected endpoints: /v1/generate; affected region: prod-us-east; estimated customer impact ~8-12% traffic window; mitigation: feature-flag flip + full canary rollback.
